text: The environment is everything that surrounds a living organism. Its components are of two kinds. Biotic components are the living things — plants, animals, and microorganisms. Abiotic components are the non-living things — air, water, soil, sunlight, and temperature. A healthy environment depends on the balance between them.
source: Seed reference: My Science Grade 6, Ch.2 Environment (authored sample, not official text)
subject: Science

text: Biotic components are grouped by how they obtain food. Producers, such as green plants, make their own food using sunlight. Consumers, such as a goat or a human, eat plants or other animals. Decomposers, such as mushrooms and bacteria, break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil.

text: Around a Nepali village you can see every component of the environment at once: the rice plant (producer) in the paddy field, the goat (consumer) grazing on it, the mushroom (decomposer) on a rotting log, and the soil, river water, and sunlight (abiotic) that support them all.
